verdict.rationale: E2B documents its own controls over how long sandboxes live. You can kill a sandbox at any time, reset its timeout, and shut down single or all sandboxes from the CLI. Paused sandboxes are kept indefinitely with no automatic deletion, so retention of paused state is user-controlled, and self-hosting offers deployment-level control. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that killing a sandbox permanently deletes its filesystem/memory data, documented deletion of paused sandboxes and snapshots, a retention policy for logs, metrics and metadata, account-level data deletion, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: You can shutdown the sandbox any time even before the timeout is up by calling the `kill` method.
When you call the set timeout method, the sandbox timeout will be reset to the new value that you specified.
A paused sandbox is kept indefinitely with no automatic deletion.
You can shutdown single or all running sandboxes with the E2B CLI.
You can manage sandbox snapshots with the `e2b sandbox snapshot` (alias `snap`) commands.
Read the self-hosting guide to learn how to set up the E2B infrastructure on your own.
